# frontmatter-schema

<!-- okfreq:index:start -->
<!-- Generated by okfreq lint; edit requirement metadata instead. -->

- [StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-001 — Frontmatter appears as a readable, configurable properties table](StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-001.md) — When a writer opens a document that starts with YAML frontmatter, the Studio SHALL show it as a properties table at the top of the preview, escaping every value, in a compact YAML-like form that fits the preview width, that follows the frontmatter settings and that refreshes in place shortly after the last edit.
- [StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-002 — Invalid frontmatter is explained and the body still renders](StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-002.md) — When a document's frontmatter is not valid YAML or is not a mapping, the Studio SHALL show an error row and badge in the properties table while still rendering the Markdown body.
- [StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-003 — Property values read like YAML](StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-003.md) — When a writer reads a properties table, the Studio SHALL show booleans, lists, null and nested values in a compact YAML-like form that fits the preview width.
- [StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-004 — The Description column can be collapsed](StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-004.md) — When a writer collapses the Description column of a properties table, the Studio SHALL keep Name and Value readable and remember the choice for that document.
- [StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-005 — Frontmatter settings control the table and apply live](StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-005.md) — When a writer changes a `frontmatter.*` setting, the Studio SHALL update the open previews without reopening them, and when `frontmatter.propertiesTable` is off SHALL show neither the table nor the raw YAML.
- [StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-006 — A document finds its schema and schema problems are reported](StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-006.md) — When a document's frontmatter has a string type, the Studio SHALL look for the matching schema file in the nearest schema folder, load it in YAML, JSON or JSON5 with its references inlined, and tell the writer when none applies or when the schema cannot be used, without hiding the metadata.
- [StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-007 — Schema files can be written in several formats and share parts](StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-007.md) — When a schema file is written in YAML, JSON or JSON5 and refers to other schema files, the Studio SHALL load it and inline the referenced parts.
- [StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-008 — Schema problems are reported without hiding the metadata](StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-008.md) — When a schema file cannot be read, parsed or compiled, the Studio SHALL show the metadata as a generic or unvalidated table together with a message that names the problem.
- [StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-009 — Schema edits are picked up on the next analysis](StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-009.md) — When a writer edits a schema file or a file it refers to, the Studio SHALL use the new content the next time the document is analysed.
- [StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-010 — Fields follow the schema and problems show on the field concerned](StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-010.md) — When a document's type has a schema, the Studio SHALL list its fields in schema order with their type, description and allowed values, mark each field that violates the schema, summarise the issues in a badge, list the missing required fields and warn on undeclared fields when the strict setting is on.
- [StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-011 — Validation problems show on the field concerned](StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-011.md) — When a document's frontmatter violates its schema, the Studio SHALL mark the field concerned, summarise the issues in a badge and list the missing required fields.
- [StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-012 — Unknown fields can be flagged](StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-012.md) — When `frontmatter.strictAdditionalProperties` is on, the Studio SHALL warn on each field that the matching schema does not declare.
- [StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-013 — The table follows edits to the document](StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-013.md) — When a writer edits the frontmatter, the Studio SHALL refresh the properties table in place shortly after the last change without reloading the preview.
- [StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-014 — Frontmatter link fields resolve, show their status and can be followed](StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-014.md) — When a schema annotates a field with x-okf-link, the Studio SHALL treat that field's values as links to files, resolve them from the matching root, show on each value whether it resolves and why not, show the linked file's evidence, and open a resolving link in the editor while refusing unusable links with a reason.
- [StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-015 — Links resolve against the right root](StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-015.md) — When a frontmatter link value is checked, the Studio SHALL resolve it by the annotation's resolution mode from the matching root and refuse targets outside the allowed folders.
- [StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-016 — Link status is visible on each value](StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-016.md) — When a frontmatter link value is displayed, the Studio SHALL show whether it resolves and, if not, why, without blocking the first paint.
- [StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-017 — Linked files show their evidence](StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-017.md) — When a frontmatter link resolves to a Markdown file, the Studio SHALL show the fields and line the annotation asks for from that file, and keep them current.
- [StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-018 — Frontmatter links can be followed](StRS-MDOKFSTUDIO-FMSCHEMA-018.md) — When a writer activates a resolving frontmatter link, the Studio SHALL open the target in the editor, at its marker line when the annotation defines one, and refuse unusable links with a reason.

<!-- okfreq:index:end -->
